purpose: EDGAR primary-verification of the R42 independent modern brine-bromine cost lead (ROADMAP q1, DOW-litmus sourcing wall). Promote the Gulf Resources Q3-2022 cost basis from UNVERIFIED-PRIMARY (press-release) to DERIVED-FROM-PRIMARY (byte-verified 10-Q inputs), and primary-verify the ICL 20-F + USGS MCS secondary bearings. Nothing here is admitted to route ranking; this is a sourcing receipt matching the R35 Magnolia primary-source standard.
verdict: PARTIAL->ADVANCED. Gulf Q3-2022 fully-absorbed cost $2.7726/kg is now DERIVED-FROM-PRIMARY (exact filing inputs, Gulf's own revenue/tonnes method, $0.00 delta vs press release). ICL 20-F confirms NO bromine-specific $/kg cost is extractable (bromine buried in the Industrial Products segment) and byte-confirms the recon IP figures. USGS MCS import CIF price series is now primary-verified ($2.70/kg 2024, $3.00/kg 2025e) but is an IMPORT PRICE, not a production cost (US production is 'W'-withheld duopoly-proprietary). No independent modern producer CASH cost exists; Gulf gives a primary-sourced fully-absorbed UPPER bound only.

gulf_resources_primary.boundary: The $2,772.60/t is a FULLY-ABSORBED accounting cost of net revenue (explicitly includes depreciation & amortization per the filing), NOT a cash cost, at 34% utilization that is itself diluted by factories 'that have not commenced operations'. It is a LOOSE UPPER BOUND on steady-state cash cost. The fixed/variable split needed to extract marginal cash cost is NOT disclosed. Gulf is a distressed micro-cap (going-concern history, late/amended filings). SEC-filed and independent, but not a representative healthy producer.
gulf_resources_primary.what_it_buys: Q3 2022 (least-distorted, 34% util) fully-absorbed cost $2.77/kg brackets the R35 Albemarle/Magnolia forecast $2.5365/kg from a completely unrelated producer - a genuine second, primary-sourced bearing on order of magnitude, implying a full-utilization cash cost plausibly below $2/kg. Corroborates the forecast magnitude WITHOUT deriving from it.

icl_group_secondary.issuer: ICL Group Ltd. (world's largest elemental-bromine manufacturer)
icl_group_secondary.independence: FULL - Israel/Dead-Sea producer, unrelated to Albemarle or Gulf
icl_group_secondary.finding: IP (Industrial Products) segment table discloses NO cost-of-sales or gross-profit line (Potash segment does: 'Gross Profit 622 650'). IP goes Sales -> Operating Income -> D&A -> EBITDA -> CapEx. The segment mixes bromine + bromine compounds + phosphorus flame retardants + magnesia + calcium carbonate + salt + MgCl2, so its only aggregate expense figure ($1,034M, FY2025) cannot be attributed to bromine. Bromine VOLUME is disclosed but no bromine-only cost/COGS/price line exists to pair with it. Dividing segment expense by bromine volume would be fabrication.

usgs_mcs_secondary.spot_verified_by_orchestrator: sha256 recomputed on all 3 PDFs=match; price line 2.70/3.00 and 'Withheld to avoid disclosing company proprietary data' greps FOUND in pdftotext extracts
usgs_mcs_secondary.correction: The recon quoted USGS 'Because the bromine industry has few producers, published price lists ... were not available.' That phrasing is from the 2018 Minerals Yearbook, NOT the modern (2024-2026) MCS chapters. The modern chapters instead withhold US production entirely ('W Withheld to avoid disclosing company proprietary data') because 'Bromine was recovered from underground brines by two companies in Arkansas' (a duopoly).
usgs_mcs_secondary.boundary: USGS 'Price' bounds what US buyers PAID for imported bromine, silent on any producer's cost of production. US domestic production is fully 'W'-withheld by design. Confirms the structural reframe: no modern production-cost reference is obtainable from USGS.
